chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Asbat from Sa'dan ibn Muslim from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man was in Medina who entered the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Allah, comfort my loneliness and connect my solitude and grant me a righteous companion.' Then he found a man in the farthest part of the mosque, so he greeted him and said to him, 'Who are you, O servant of Allah?' He said, 'I am Abu Dharr.' The man said, 'Allah is Great! Allah is Great!' Abu Dharr said, 'And why do you exclaim, O servant of Allah?' He said, 'I entered the mosque and supplicated to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to comfort my loneliness and connect my solitude and grant me a righteous companion.' Abu Dharr said to him, 'I have more right to exclaim than you if I am that companion, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: I and you will be upon a canal on the Day of Resurrection until the people finish from the accounting. Arise, O servant of Allah, for the Sultan has prohibited sitting with me.'
ai.seo_question: Who is the companion of the Prophet that answered a man's prayer for a righteous friend in Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia concept of *tawassul* through the intercession of the Ahl al-Bayt and the Companions, specifically highlighting Abu Dharr al-Ghifari as a model of righteous companionship (*sahib al-salih*). The narrative underscores the tension between spiritual merit and political marginalization, as Abu Dharr attributes his seclusion to the ruling authority's prohibition, a theme resonant with the broader Shia historical experience of the *Ulama* and Imams under various caliphates. It serves as a practical lesson for believers to seek out and maintain bonds with the pious, even when they are socially or politically isolated.

en.hubeali: H 14926 – Al-Husayn Bin Muhammad Al-Ashary, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Sa’daan Bin Muslim, from some of our companions, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws having said:

‘There was a man in Al-Medina who entered the Masjid of the Messenger<sup>saww</sup> and he said, ‘Grant me comfort in my anxiety, and company for my loneliness, and sustenance of a righteous companion’. There was a man seated in the corner of the Masjid. So he greeted him and said to him, ‘Who are you, O servant of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>?’ So he<sup>ar</sup> said: ‘I<sup>ar</sup> am Abu Dharr<sup>ar</sup>’. The man said, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Great! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Great!’ So Abu Dharr<sup>ar</sup> said: ‘And why did you exclaim that, O servant of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>?’ He said, ‘I entered the Masjid, so I supplicated to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic to Grant me comfort in my anxiety, and company for my loneliness, and sustenance of a righteous companion’. So Abu Dharr<sup>ar</sup> said to him, ‘I<sup>ar</sup> have more right for the exclamation than you are if I<sup>ar</sup> was that companion, for I<sup>ar</sup> heard the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup> saying: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> and you<sup>ar</sup> would be upon a canal on the Day of Judgement until the people are free from the Accounting. Arise (and leave) O servant of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> for the authorities have prohibited for anyone to be seated with me<sup>ar</sup>’.
